faqs.q: What is the Bent Hitch Pin and what is it used for?
faqs.a: The Bent Hitch Pin is a retaining pin listed in 6 sizes, 3/8″ to 3/4″. Retaining pins keep a clevis pin, bolt or hitch pin in place. They are quick to fit and remove, and they stop the pin they retain working loose. Browse the range on our [rigging pins shelf](/c/rigging-pins).

faqs.q: What sizes does the Bent Hitch Pin come in?
faqs.a: The Bent Hitch Pin comes in 6 sizes, 3/8″ to 3/4″. The table starts at 1/2″ and runs up to 5/8″. Every size has its own Indus part number, with its dimensions in the size table. If your size is not listed, send the load, pin or rope size and we will confirm what fits.

faqs.q: How do I size the Bent Hitch Pin for a job?
faqs.a: Pick the Bent Hitch Pin on the rated load for the pull you will actually apply, then check the pin and hole it retains. These retainers do not carry the load; replace one that is bent or has lost its spring. The smallest listed is 1/2″. See our [guide to lynch pins, R-clips and wire lock pins](/blog/lynch-pins-r-clips-and-wire-lock-pins) for more.

faqs.q: What load can the Bent Hitch Pin carry?
faqs.a: No working load limit applies to the Bent Hitch Pin, because it is a retainer and does not carry the load. The load is carried by the clevis pin, bolt or hitch pin it secures, so rate that part and size this pin to its hole. Replace a retainer that is bent or has lost its spring.

faqs.q: How do I order a specific size of the Bent Hitch Pin?
faqs.a: Quote the Indus part number from the size table, for example IH-LR-RP-BHP-050-ZP—12 for the 1/2″ size or IH-LR-RP-BHP-062-SS—LP for the 5/8″ size. Add the quantity and, if you need more than the standard paperwork, say so on the request. If you only know the load and the pin or rope size, send those and we will match the part number.

faqs.q: How does the Bent Hitch Pin compare with the Lynch Pin?
faqs.a: The Bent Hitch Pin and the Lynch Pin belong to the same family but differ in type, size and material, so their ratings and fit are not interchangeable. The Bent Hitch Pin is listed in 6 sizes, 3/8″ to 3/4″. Compare the rating or size marked on each part, not the name, before substituting one for the other. See the [Lynch Pin](/p/lynch-pin) for its own sizes.

faqs.q: What is the Bent Hitch Pin made of?
faqs.a: The Bent Hitch Pin is an electro-galvanized bent pin fastener, and the size table also lists a stainless steel lynch-pin version. Zinc plating or galvanizing protects carbon steel from rust, though the coating wears with use. Tell us the working environment if you need a different material or finish.

faqs.q: What standard and certificate come with the Bent Hitch Pin?
faqs.a: The manufacturer's data lists the Bent Hitch Pin as stamped, and no load rating or lifting standard applies to a retaining pin. Ask on your request for any documents you need, such as a test certificate.

faqs.q: What can the Bent Hitch Pin be connected to?
faqs.a: The Bent Hitch Pin retains clevis pins, bolts, hitch pins; match its diameter to the hole in the pin or bolt. Fit it through the cross hole of the part it retains and check that it seats fully and holds. It keeps the other pin in place but is not what carries the load. Related: [shackles](/c/shackles).

faqs.q: How do I inspect the Bent Hitch Pin before use?
faqs.a: Check the Bent Hitch Pin each time it is fitted: it should sit fully through its hole, hold firmly and show no bending, corrosion or loss of spring. Our [guide](/blog/lynch-pins-r-clips-and-wire-lock-pins) covers it in more detail.

faqs.q: Where is the Bent Hitch Pin typically used?
faqs.a: The Bent Hitch Pin is used to keep a clevis pin, bolt or hitch pin from working loose on trailers, rigging, shackles and plant. Sizes run 3/8″ to 3/4″. It is a retainer, not a load-bearing part.
